memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The angel of the Lord also said to her: "You are now pregnant and you will give birth to a son. You shall name him Ishmael, for the Lord has heard of your misery." - Gen 16:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Hagar to name her son Ishmael, which means "God hears." And He gives the reason: "for the Lord has heard of your misery." Every time Hagar would call her son's name - thousands of times over the years - she would be reminded: God heard me. God listened to my suffering. My cries did not vanish into the empty desert.

Think about what this meant to her. Hagar was a slave; no one asked her opinion, no one cared about her pain. Sarai mistreated her, Abram abandoned her, and she fled in silent misery. But God heard. The One whom everyone else ignored was listening all along.

This is one of the most comforting truths in all of Scripture: God hears the cries of the miserable and the mistreated. Your suffering is not invisible to Him. Even when you have no words, even when no one else notices, even when your pain seems to disappear into silence - God hears.

The Bible returns to this again and again: "The Lord hears the needy" (Ps 69:33); "This poor man called, and the Lord heard him" (Ps 34:6). And supremely, God so heard the misery of a lost world that He sent His Son to answer it. Whatever misery you carry today, name it before God. He has heard, and He is not silent toward those who suffer.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God hears your misery, even when no one else does?
- What suffering do you need to bring to the God who hears?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You hear my misery even when no one else does, even when I have no words. My suffering is not invisible to You. I bring You my pain today, trusting that You have heard.
Amen.
